title: Reliability Interface Charter and 90d Experiment Catalog
content:
Purpose: quick operational charter to define how SRE, product, serving-runtime, and platform teams make decisions about SLOs, error budgets, and short experiments over the next 90 days. This doc is intentionally lightweight: a decision protocol + experiment catalog + daily/weekly rituals to reduce friction during launches and SLO tuning.

Background (tl;dr): we have frequent tensions when service owners change model configs, caching, or batch settings that affect tail latency or error-rate. Root causes are unclear ownership of SLO trade-offs, inconsistent experiment guardrails, and slow feedback loops for regressions. This charter establishes a small cross-functional interface and a series of timeboxed experiments to validate operational levers.

Core principles (working):
- Minimize blast radius: every experiment must state rollback criteria and be reversible in <4 hours.
- Surface economics: link change to estimated per-token cost delta, not just latency.
- Fast feedback: prefer short canary windows and synthetic workloads that approximate production patterns.
- Targeted visibility: require specific dashboards and alert rules for each experiment.

Interface: who talks to whom when a change touches SLOs
- SRE point (interface owner): Aisha Patel (primary), Diego Martinez (backup).
- Product steward: Riley Chen (hosted-api product).
- Serving runtime lead: Samira Khan.
- Platform eng contact: Luke Brennan.
- Communication channel: #reliability-interface (Slack) and the confluence page above for artifacts.

Decision protocol (short):
1) Proposal: service owner files a lightweight RFC in Confluence and a JIRA ticket tagged REL-EX (template below). Include hypothesis, estimated risk, rollback, dashboards, and cost delta.
2) Rapid review: SRE + product + runtime review within 48 hours. If low risk, greenlight for a 48–72h canary. If medium risk, schedule a 1-hour sync and define extra safety gates. If high risk, escalate to reliability council.
3) Canary & observe: run canary, collect metrics (see metric bundle), maintain live notes in the JIRA ticket.
4) Decision: within the canary window, decide to promote, iterate, or rollback. Use the documented success/rollback criteria.

Metric bundle (mandatory per experiment):
- SLOs: p99 latency (in ms), availability/error-rate (% of failed requests), and request success SLA (if present).
- Cost signals: per-token GPU time (ms/token), estimated $/1M tokens.
- Experience signals: client timeouts, queued requests, controller errors.
- Instrumentation: include trace ids for 5 representative traces, synthetic workload traces and KV cache hit-rate.

Experiment catalog (90d) — concise entries (owner, hypothesis, metrics, success, rollback, schedule):
1) Name: adaptive-small-batches (owner: Samira Khan)
   Hypothesis: reducing dynamic batch size ceiling from 64->32 for latency-sensitive routes will lower p99 by ~20% with <3% throughput loss.
   Metrics: p99 latency, throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, per-token cost estimate.
   Success: p99 down >=15% and cost per token delta <= +5%.
   Rollback: automatic if p99 increases or throughput drops >10% for 15m.
   Schedule: canary for route /v1/chat with 1% traffic for 72h.

2) Name: prefix-kv-cache-ttl-probe (owner: Diego Martinez)
   Hypothesis: shortening prefix KV cache TTL from 30m->5m will reduce KV staleness-induced misses and improve tail latency under multi-tenant noisy workloads.
   Metrics: KV hit rate, p95/p99, backend egress, memory pressure.
   Success: KV hit rate improves for targeted tenant subset and p99 down >=10%.
   Rollback: revert TTL if memory pressure >80% of nodes or p99 worsens by 5% for 30m.
   Schedule: bench + 48h isolated smoke + 48h canary.

3) Name: lightweight-quantization-shadow (owner: Riley Chen)
   Hypothesis: running quantized model variant in shadow for identical requests will reveal quality delta while measuring latency/cost differences without exposing users.
   Metrics: token-level output similarity score (cosine on embedding of tokens), CPU/GPU time, memory.
   Success: similarity >=0.985 on eval prompt set and p99 latency benefit >=10% in shadow.
   Rollback: N/A (shadow only) but gate promotion on quality audits.
   Schedule: 2 week shadow run + weekly quality review.

4) Name: routing-fallback-fastpath (owner: Luke Brennan)
   Hypothesis: adding a fastpath route for requests under 128 tokens to small-model pool will reduce latency SLO pressure without affecting error budgets.
   Metrics: route-level p50/p95/p99, error budget consumption, inter-pool saturation.
   Success: route-level p99 improves by 25% and global error budget burn unchanged.
   Rollback: remove route if inter-pool error budget burn increases >5% in 1h.
   Schedule: 48h canary at 0.5% traffic, then 7d staged ramp.

Operational templates (cut-paste into RFC):
- RFC title — short
- Owner + backup
- Route(s) affected
- Hypothesis (one sentence)
- Success criteria (quantitative)
- Rollback criteria (quantitative)
- Dashboards and panels (links)
- Estimated cost impact (delta $/M tokens)
- Safety gates (feature flags, rate-limits)

Weekly rituals and quick syncs:
- Mon 09:30 15m async notes: status updates, blockers (owner: Aisha)
- Wed 11:00 30m review: SRE + product + runtime (rotate lead) — decide on promotions/rollbacks
- Friday 10:00 60m deep-dive: experiment results, learnings, next-90d re-prioritization (attendees: all collaborators)

Escalation ladders (when to call the reliability council):
- If cumulative error budget burn for a product >50% in 72h and projected to exceed 100% in 7d.
- If a canary fails safety gates and rollback does not restore baseline within 4 hours.
- If a change causes more than 2 production incidents in a rolling 7d window.

Runbook pointers (to attach to each experiment):
- quick-rollback commands (CLI) — list commands and owners
- warm standby steps for region failover
- how to attach a temporary throttling rule via edge router
- link to incident template and P0 channel playbook

Open questions / items to resolve (short)
- Do we need an explicit financial approver for experiments with >10% projected cost increase? (action: product finance to advise; ticket: JIRA-PROD-4210)
- What is the exact p99 budget allocation per product line? We have coarse budgets now; need per-route mapping. (owner: Riley)
- Instrumentation gaps: missing trace sampling for batched requests — SRE to propose minimal sampling change. (owner: Diego)

Quick TODOs (near-term):
- [ ] Add adaptive-small-batches to JIRA and attach dashboards (owner: Samira)
- [ ] Create quantization shadow eval checklist and baseline prompt set (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Add runbook links to each RFC template (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Schedule Wed review and invite runtime/plat rotation (owner: Aisha)

Notes-to-self / heuristics:
- If experiment affects p99 but leaves p95 intact, treat as a tail distribution problem and expect shaky telemetry; run an extended canary for 7 days.
- Prefer shadow + small canary before full promotion; production exposure should be incremental and measurable.
- Document small wins: even 5–10% p99 improvement on a critical route can unlock cost optimizations.

Appendix: example minimal RFC blurb (paste into Confluence):
"Title: adaptive-small-batches for /v1/chat
Owner: Samira Khan (SRE: Aisha Patel)
Summary: reduce batch ceiling for latency-sensitive route to improve tail latency.
Hypothesis: p99 down >=15% with <5% cost increase.
Success: p99 down >=15% in 72h canary; error budget burn <= baseline.
Rollback: auto-revert if p99 > baseline or throughput drop >10% for 15m.
Dashboards: <link>
Jira: JIRA-OPS-4129"

Last note: this doc is meant to be messy and pragmatic. If you copy it, please mark edits — the single-sourced runbook should live in Confluence once we stabilize the first two experiments.

Revision history: 2026-12-10 initial sketch by Aisha; 2026-12-15 added experiment owners and schedules (Diego, Samira); 2026-12-20 clarified decision protocol and added TODOs (Riley).
